5.0.s.en: (1) The problem of fornication and how the Apostle dealt with it

5.0.0.en: One of the believers in Corinth sinned by committing fornication with his father's wife. This sin is against sound human nature and is rare even among unbelievers, so how much more shameful is the fall of one of the believers into it!

5.1.0.en: Here the Apostle Paul returns to what he had already pointed out, the boasting of the Corinthians in their spiritual virtues, and asks: how can you claim knowledge and wisdom for yourselves, when you should rather have been ashamed when you heard that such an abomination had occurred among you? You did not rebuke yourselves and mourn for the disgrace you brought upon the Church, which ought to be pure like its Lord. Instead of being proud, you ought to have removed the one who committed this iniquity from among you.

5.2.0.en: Paul was in Ephesus when he wrote this epistle, but that did not prevent him from considering and judging the matter of the one among the members of the church of Corinth who committed this act, as though he were present among them in spirit, thinking of them, caring for their success and suffering for every harm that befell them. He had the right and the authority which he received from the Lord Jesus, and he reckoned the members of the Church to be gathered together and himself to be among them in spirit.

5.3.0.en: Paul pronounced judgment that he be cut off and deprived of the Church and of partaking of the Holy Mysteries, in the hope that he would repent when he suffered from this deprivation and became aware of the horror of his sin, and so repent; then the Church would receive him and he would regain the purity of his body and spirit, and be saved on the day of judgment.

5.3.1.en: This shows that the authority of excommunication from the Church is an apostolic tradition and a scriptural commandment, since the Apostles and the priests, their successors, have the right to this action if circumstances require it. The source of authority to cut someone off from the Church is the Lord Jesus, who declared that it is necessary, and the one who commanded that it be carried out is the Apostle Paul. This Church discipline always turns to benefit, and if the person accepts it and repents, he escapes eternal judgment.

5.3.2.en: This abominable sin did not happen suddenly but is the result of gradual negligence. So watch the beginnings of sins, such as a look, a thought or an emotional inclination, so that you do not defile yourself, for all of these are stages of fornication; and give up any of them however beloved, and keep away from whoever encourages you in it.

5.4.s.en: (2) The necessity of purging the Church of the corrupt

5.4.0.en: You boast of your wisdom and your spiritual gifts, but this has no real basis, because your condition calls for shame and for fear of the spread of evil as a result of the error of one member of your church, whom others will imitate. To explain this, the Apostle Paul uses the idea that a small amount of leaven is able to leaven a large amount of dough, to warn them that just as one sin, if its doer does not repent, opens many doors before him to commit other sins, so sin spreads from one person to another within the community. If someone transgresses the commandments of God and is not rebuked, disciplined and set apart, others imitate him and make light of iniquity.

5.5.0.en: It is therefore your duty to remove the person who sinned from your midst, and to cleanse yourselves and your church community of the corruption that has accompanied human nature since the Fall, so that you become pure, renewed and holy, purged of sin, as unleavened bread is free of leaven. Just as the Jews purified themselves at the Passover according to the Mosaic law, when they slaughtered the Passover lamb and went on eating unleavened bread for seven days in the feast of unleavened bread, which signifies the whole of life, so also, since Christ has been slaughtered for us and has become our Passover, we must purge ourselves of every evil.

5.6.0.en: So let your whole life be holy to God, as a perpetual holy feast, with a pure, renewed nature and not, as before, a corrupt human nature. The corrupt nature is liable to evil and malice, but the renewed nature is a nature sincere in its purity and its good, blameless conduct, and loving all that is true. Sincerity points to holiness of conduct and behavior, and truth points to holiness of spiritual doctrine and faith.

5.6.1.en: God was sincere in His love for you and died to redeem you, and He cares for you every day. Are you sincere toward Him and do you strive to please Him? Do you refuse every evil that angers Him, and rejoice in being often with Him in prayers and readings?

5.7.s.en: (3) The Church has the right to judge its members

5.7.0.en: I wrote to you before, in (vv. 1, 2), to keep away from fornicators. But I never meant that you should withdraw from the fornicators of this world, that is, from unbelievers, or from the covetous who desire to gain wealth by any means, whether justly or unjustly, or from extortioners, who wrong others by taking more than is their right, or from idolaters, who worship false gods. For if I had meant to forbid you to associate with such people, it would be as if I were commanding you to depart to another world than this one, because such people are found everywhere in the world, and we must deal with them in the transactions necessary for life.

5.8.0.en: And now I make clearer to you what I meant when I wrote to you before. If anyone claims to be a Christian and has entered into the fellowship of the Church but is a fornicator, or covetous, or an idolater, or a reviler of others, or drinks wine excessively to the point of drunkenness, or wrongs others, I tell you: keep away from this person; for if he is defiled by the corruption that is in the world and the Church nevertheless keeps him in its midst, it is as if it allows the world to enter it, which makes the Church lose its spirituality and holiness and everything by which it is distinguished of truth and purity.

5.9.0.en: It is not for me or for you to judge those who are outside the Church, but those who are inside the Church.

5.10.0.en: As for those outside the Church, God alone judges them, whether in the present world or on the last day. It is your right, indeed your duty, to separate the one who walks in evil and malice among you.

5.10.1.en: Open your heart in love to every person and pray for those who are far away and for sinners, but do not mingle or associate with the wicked and become accustomed to sitting with them and amusing yourself with them, lest you be swept along into their sins. Be humble and careful, and God will keep you from sin.

6.0.s.en: (1) The prohibition against resorting to pagan courts

6.0.0.en: "Dare any of you, having a matter against another", such as a disagreement over dividing money, property or an inheritance, go to law before the pagans? The Apostle Paul called them "the unjust" because they violated the law of righteousness by their worship of idols and their denial of the true God, and in contrast he called the believers "saints". Through this astonished question, the Apostle Paul considered it a disgrace for Christians to be unable to settle the disputes of the brethren and to resort to pagan courts to judge between them.

6.1.0.en: You know perfectly well that your conduct as believers will judge the world that did not believe. The sitting of the saints with Christ for judgment confirms that He considered them worthy to judge. If believers are worthy to judge on the day of judgment, they are all the more worthy to judge in worldly matters, those concerning money and what relates to it, which are very small matters compared with the matters of the day of judgment. This is why the Church holds to having a special law for the personal status of Christians.

6.2.0.en: You also know, from Christian teaching, that you will judge the angels who fell, that is, the demons, on the day of judgment, for their refusal to submit to God (Jude 2, 6 Pet 3:4). All the more are you worthy to judge people in temporal matters.

6.3.0.en: Here the Apostle's words carry the sense of astonishment and rebuke. By "those who are least esteemed" is meant those of less standing. So set them as judges among you, for the least among you understands the commandments of God better than the pagans of the world.

6.4.0.en: I say this to make you ashamed of your improper conduct. It is a great disgrace for those who claim wisdom that they find no wise man among them fit to judge between the brethren (how is this, is there not a wise man among you?). Therefore they are compelled to resort to the pagan courts.

6.5.0.en: How can a brother accept being taken to court by his brother over the matters of this life before pagan judges? The Holy Bible does not mean here to reject the authority of the civil courts, for it calls us to submit to the rulers and authorities of the world (Rom 13:1-5), but it is a call to reconciliation in all cases under the guidance of respected spiritual men and those of experience in the Church.

6.5.1.en: Would that when we differ with one another over material matters we resort to understanding and prayer and readiness to give up some rights for the sake of love. And if we do not agree, let us return to the Church in the person of its fathers and guides, so that they may decide between us in these material matters, which are less important than the spiritual matters in which they guide us; and thus we keep our love for one another. Let us put love and peace above the love of material things.

6.6.0.en: It is a fault in you that there are lawsuits among you over the matters of this worldly life. Why do you not prefer to bear wrong and not seek to resort to the courts? Material loss is nothing beside the loss of brotherly love.

6.7.0.en: He rebukes them for wronging one another, which leads the wronged to resort to the civil courts, whereas Christian principles urge them to love the brethren as members in one body and in the fellowship of the one Church.

6.7.1.en: Would that we imitate Christ, who suffered for us: "who, when He was reviled, reviled not again; when He suffered, He threatened not; but committed Himself to Him that judgeth righteously" (1 Pet 2:23).

6.8.s.en: (2) The sins that deprive one of the Kingdom

6.8.0.en: "Know ye not that the unrighteous shall not inherit the kingdom of God?" There is no doubt that you knew that whoever wrongs others has no inheritance in the Kingdom of Heaven. And know that the vices mentioned next prevent entry into the Kingdom, because most of those who were around them, of the pagans, committed them without any reproach of conscience. These vices are: fornication, idolatry, prostitution, and falling into sexual perversion ("effeminate": those who lie with males), theft, covetousness, drunkenness, reviling and extortion, that is, taking what they have no right to. And to show them how their condition changed when they became Christians, Paul reminded them that they used to practice those vices before in their pagan society, but now he says to them: you are completely separated from the former evils, for you have been purified and washed in the sacrament of Baptism and consecrated to Christ in the Myron, and you were reckoned righteous by what Christ did for you and by the work of the Holy Spirit in you.

6.8.1.en: Always remember your new, pure nature which you received in Baptism, so that you keep away from sin and do not share in it with the people of the world. And do not forget that you are consecrated to God in your heart, your senses and your thoughts, so that you remember His word and seek Him in all His gifts and in the events that pass over you.

6.9.s.en: (3) Do not be enslaved to the demands of the flesh

6.9.0.en: The Apostle Paul raises us to a new spiritual degree, so that we refrain not only from evil but also from things that are permitted, eating of them only what agrees with and suits our life in God. Just as a person understands that for every occasion he wears the clothing suited to it, so many things do not suit the spiritual man although they are not sins in themselves and may be used in special cases, such as drinking wine, which was used anciently as a medicine in some cases, or the stripping of solitary ascetics, who wear few clothes, but this nakedness does not suit ordinary life.

6.9.1.en: And more than this, a person must not be attached to any material thing so that it comes to dominate him, whether food or drink or anything material.

6.10.0.en: The belly was created in man to receive food, and God created both for man's benefit and bodily need and to obtain strength to fulfill his obligations toward God and society. But this arrangement is temporary for life on earth and ends with the end of his temporal life, for in eternity there is no eating or drinking. It is true that the belly is for foods and foods for the belly, but a person must not be a slave to his belly, and likewise the body must not be for fornication, because God did not create the body of man to commit fornication; the body belongs to the Lord, and Christ bought us with His blood. The pagans thought, as some wicked people like them also say now, that fornication is a natural need of man. Of course this is evil, and God did not create the body for fornication, that is, for bodily relations outside marriage.

6.11.0.en: God cares for the body, and since He rose as the firstfruits of them that slept, He honored His body, which is like our bodies, and He will raise them glorified at the second coming. So it is not permissible for a person to defile his body by fornication.

6.12.s.en: (4) Our bodies are temples of the Holy Spirit

6.12.0.en: You know that the bodies of believers are members of the body of Christ, which is the Church, for they partake of His most holy Body and Blood, so they are His and are His members. Is it fitting, then, for any believer among us to take the members of Christ and make them members of a harlot? Paul utterly rejects this by saying, "God forbid."

6.13.0.en: A man's union with his wife makes the two one flesh, as the Scripture says: "A man shall leave his father and mother, and shall cleave unto his wife: and they shall be one flesh" (Gen 2:24). So he who is joined to a harlot becomes one body with the harlot, and the two become partners in one defiled and hateful life, which does not befit one who has become a member of Christ, for by this he separates himself from membership in the Church.

6.14.0.en: But he that is joined unto the Lord becomes one spirit with Him, that is, he is filled with the Spirit of God, who is the Holy Spirit, and walks in complete obedience to Him and refrains from everything that is contrary to this glorious union. This is why God forbade fornication, because it is not a sphere of love and holy unity, but a sphere in which each party exploits the other to satisfy his lusts.

6.15.0.en: Refrain completely from everything that can lead to committing the sin of fornication. All the sins of the heart, such as hatred, envy, reviling, lying and others, do not defile the body of the one who commits them, but fornication corrupts the body as well as corrupting the spirit, because the fornicator uses his body contrary to God's purpose in creating the body, in addition to his corrupting the physical, mental and moral powers of man, and it is often the cause of serious diseases.

6.16.0.en: As I made clear to you before and you know well, your bodies are Christ's and the dwelling of the Holy Spirit which God gives you, so they are for God and not for man.

6.17.0.en: For Christ redeemed you and bought you with His precious blood, and this great price with which God was pleased to redeem man is proof of the value of the human soul to God.

6.17.1.en: So glorify God for your redemption and for the greatness of the price with which you were bought, by dedicating your bodies as temples for the indwelling of the Holy Spirit and by keeping them pure, and by keeping your spirits in the love of God and obedience to Him, for it is the breath of life whose source is God, as the Scripture says: "And the Lord God formed man of the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life" (Gen 2:7).

6.17.2.en: Let us reflect on our persons, spirit and body, to know that they are a trust deposited with us which we will return to their Owner, who is God, so we have no right to defile them. And let us guard our senses, which are the entrance of sin, so that our bodies remain pure, and let us fill them with spiritual things, such as looking at the icons of the saints, repeating the prayers, and hearing spiritual words along with reading the Holy Bible.
